analysis.title: Dealers Most Short Gamma Since 2019 As McElligott Braces For NVDA-Anthropic-OpEx "Risk Quad-fecta"
key_insights: Nomura's Charlie McElligott says aggregate SPX dealer gamma fell to negative $7.3B after a multi-day drawdown, the deepest reading on Nomura's chart back to January 2019 and below the 2023 and 2024 troughs.
Negative dealer gamma means dealers sell into dips and buy into rallies, which amplifies moves. A 1.5% Monday relief rally was largely reversed by Tuesday lunch.

McElligott calls the regime 'Two-Way Accelerant Risk'. With futures near 7,320, he sees the S&P in a month either through 6500 ('without a net') or at 7800 heading to 8k. The article's napkin math puts that at roughly 11% down versus 9% up.

The calendar stacks four catalysts: NVDA earnings Tuesday night, VIX expiration Wednesday, Anthropic IPO pricing Wednesday and first trading Thursday, and monthly OpEx Friday. McElligott says they could mark a vol inflection point with substantial vanna impact.
Friday's expiry will not clear the risk because many SPX downside hedges dealers are short to customers are for December expiration, leaving residual sensitivity to any vol reset.

McElligott does not expect a VIX 30+ blowout, citing 'No Juice to Squeeze'. Leveraged VIX ETN assets are $1.3B (25th percentile) and VIX vega to be bought on a 10-point vol spike is $25M (4th percentile), versus over $100M at several points in the past two years.

He sees front-month VIX futures at about 20-22, spot VIX in the low 20s and VVIX at 110-120 as appropriate for now. A VIX move back to 17-18 could trigger lumpy mechanical equity buying that hurts underinvested, VaR-constrained investors (a 'Buyers are Higher' pain trade).
Nomura's rebalance grid shows options dealers, levered ETFs and vol control funds would sell about $82B on a 5% down day and buy about $66B on a 5% up day.

Options-implied distribution is pricing fatter left tails on a tightening in financial conditions. McElligott's fat-tail list: higher real rates and wider credit spreads, negative wealth effect, hawkish central bank repricing (Fed speaker dispute with Chair Warsh adding nearly two hikes to Spring 2027 pricing, plus an Iran supply shock), debt and equity supply from AI capex financing and record G10 deficits, and AI-geopolitical cyber risk.

Equities are $74T, or 48% of US household net assets, an all-time high above the dot-com peak (Fed Financial Accounts). Nearly $10T of the gain came in Q2. McElligott frames stocks as the main transmission channel from financial conditions to the real economy.

Nvidia, which McElligott calls the 'Central Bank of AI', is a fat-tail risk: Jensen Huang resigned November 12, CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO, and the stock is down about 35% over the past month and a half. Huang said he would return if the board asks, but per the WSJ the board is not considering it.

McElligott does not expect interim management to 'kitchen sink' tonight's quarter, saying numbers and guidance were already set. The Q&A on circular financing and China sales bans matters more than the quarter.
Nomura's options desk flagged buyers of 15.5k AMZN Feb 295/350 call spreads, 20k INTC Sep 95 calls (the third 20k INTC call buy in a week) and 8.8k MU Feb 920/1000 call spreads.

At a macro dinner, consensus was higher stocks and higher Treasury yields into year-end and a year out, with only one 'stocks down' and one 'rates lower' view. Crude consensus was also higher. Passive, target-allocation and 401(k) investors keep buying dips while professionals have been through momentum and crowding deleveraging.

Positioning is washed out: Street prime broker net leverage at zero to low single digits, systematic equity exposure at the 10th percentile after $116B of selling in two weeks, Mag7 call skew at the 12th percentile and SPX call skew at the 22nd.

Retail and passive flows are strong: EPFR showed $98.3B of global equity inflows (99.9th percentile since 2000) and $63.6B into US equities (99.7th percentile) last week. Historically, 1-week global inflows above the 97.9th percentile preceded an average 13.8% S&P gain over 12 months with an 85% hit rate.
Buybacks remain a volatility-suppressing bid. Apple has repurchased $840B over a decade and is up 30% YTD, with over $114B of authorization left at Apple and $99B at Nvidia (Bloomberg).

The same dip-buying conditioning is the risk: investors averaging down into bounces that fail create 'Sellers are Lower' risk, tied to the stacking of NVDA, AI, hawkish repricing and geopolitical risks.
During the note's writing, someone sold 13k SPX Nov 7500 puts at 203, returning roughly $1B of gamma to dealers, alongside a 50-point futures rally off the lows.

tension_points.bull_case: If vol cools after NVDA and the Anthropic IPO, a VIX drop to 17-18 could trigger lumpy mechanical buying, and passive flows, record EPFR inflows, buybacks and washed-out pro positioning support a 'Buyers are Higher' rally toward 7800-8000.
tension_points.bear_case: Dealer gamma at -$7.3B, $82B of potential selling on a 5% down day and stacked fat tails (rates, hawkish Fed repricing, Iran, AI supply, NVDA turmoil) could push the S&P through 6500.
tension_points.what_invalidates: S&P through 6500 invalidates the bull case. A failed NVDA or Anthropic IPO outcome this week would raise the odds of that.

tension_points.bull_case: Little vol short positioning and tiny dealer VIX gamma ($25M vega to buy on a 10-point spike) means no accelerant for a VIX 30+ spike, so VIX in the low 20s is appropriate.
tension_points.bear_case: A Dec 2018-style spot crash could still force a vol shock, and the stacked catalysts could act as a vol inflection point with vanna impact.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Spot index prices crashing further in a 'Dec 2018' re-do would invalidate the no-blowout view.

theme_stances.key_argument: Dealers are short gamma at extremes, so small moves no longer stay small and the S&P faces two-way accelerant risk.
Nvidia's role as the perceived put on the AI complex has been damaged by the CEO resignation and circular financing scrutiny.
Professional positioning is washed out while passive and retail flows keep buying dips, creating a Buyers are Higher dynamic into rallies.
